ticket: PL-13 — Secret-access gate: clear the four boundary violations on fix/pl-04-pipeline-defects
goal: Make `npm run check:secret-access` exit 0 on fix/pl-04-pipeline-defects, resolving each of the four violations at its own source rather than by widening the gate: the red-team driver's three lines go through the central config loader (and os.homedir()), and the read-only guard's test — the one file where reading the raw environment IS the behavior under test — gets a single, commented ALLOWLIST entry.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `npm run check:secret-access` exits 0 against the working tree on this branch and prints "Secret-access gate passed."

Each of the four reported violations is resolved by its stated mechanism: apps/web/.claude/skills/redteam-ux/driver.mjs contains no process.env access at all (the former lines 40, 41, 46), and scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs line 233 is unchanged — exempted only by the ALLOWLIST entry.

scripts/check-secret-access.mjs's ALLOWLIST grows by exactly one entry; no other file becomes exempt. EXCLUDED_SEGMENT, SOURCE_EXTENSION, DIRECT_FORBIDDEN, and every other detection pattern in that file are unchanged, and the file still imports only Node built-ins (the CI step runs before npm ci).

The new ALLOWLIST entry carries a comment naming what that file legitimately reads (the parent environment, spread into a spawned child so the guard's module-load os.tmpdir() resolves TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR under test control), stating that no secret-class value is read, and citing the precedent it follows (the org-secret gate's jiraConnectionStore.rls.test.ts entry).
`npm run test:secret-access` and `npm run test:readonly-guard` both pass.

The driver still works: node --check passes on it; with nothing set, findChrome() returns an existing Chrome/Edge executable on this machine; with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH pointing at an existing file, that path wins. Its header `Env:` line and its not-found message both name PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH.

Nothing outside the two Affected files is modified — in particular packages/config/src/config.ts, scripts/check-secret-access.test.mjs, scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs, .github/workflows/ci.yml, and docs/PRD_Tickets.md.

edgeCases.text: PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH set to an empty or whitespace-only value: getOptionalConfig throws ConfigError (validateValue's empty check), where the old `process.env.CHROME_PATH && …` was merely falsy. The wrapper must swallow ConfigError and fall through to the candidate list — never crash the driver.

PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH set to a path that does not exist: unchanged behavior — fall through to the candidate list, and if nothing matches, exit 1 with the not-found message naming the variable that actually works now.

Non-Windows host: the homedir()-derived candidate simply fails existsSync and is skipped, exactly as today's join('', 'Google\\Chrome\\…') relative path does. No crash, no behavior change on Linux/macOS.

@sayre/config does not resolve from apps/web/.claude/skills/redteam-ux/, or packages/config/dist/index.js is absent and an ordinary npm install does not produce it: the loader route is genuinely unavailable to this file. Fallback: revert the driver edit, add apps/web/.claude/skills/redteam-ux/driver.mjs to the ALLOWLIST with a comment recording the true reason (loader not resolvable from this location; reads a browser path and a Windows profile path, no secret-class value), and record the deviation in changes.md. Do not leave a half-applied edit, and do not write the "cannot import from .mjs" rationale unless it has actually been verified.

Accepted residual: an ALLOWLIST entry is whole-file and permanent, so a later edit to scripts/guard-checker-readonly.test.mjs could read a genuinely secret-class value from process.env and this gate would stay silent. Mitigants, stated rather than claimed away: (a) the justifying comment names the one sanctioned access, so a diff adding a second one is visibly outside it at review; (b) the file is a test for the read-only guard, has no production import path, and runs in CI where no real credential is provisioned; (c) the sibling check-org-secret-access.mjs gate still covers that file for the Jira raw-column class. Nothing mechanically narrows an ALLOWLIST entry to a line or a variable name today.

The new comment must not itself trip the gate. javascriptLexicalView blanks // comments before matching, so a comment spelling out the forbidden form is safe — but the gate scans its own file, so AC-1's actual run is the proof, not this reasoning.

scripts/check-secret-access.test.mjs's 'allows only the four exact loader paths' test builds fixture repos and never asserts the ALLOWLIST's size, so a fifth entry cannot break it. Its name stays accurate about what it tests — the gate does still allow exactly those four loader paths; the new entry is not a loader. Renaming it is out of scope.

The gate runs before npm ci in CI. check-secret-access.mjs must stay built-ins-only (this change adds no import to it), and the driver's new @sayre/config import is irrelevant to that step, which never executes the driver.
